_readme: Committed p95 latency budgets for the nightly-load-test CI job (#1082). See docs/development/nightly-load-test.md for the full contract: fixture size, budget-derivation rule, and how to re-derive this file at each release. DO NOT hand-edit budget_p95_ms to a round number — every value here must trace to a measured_p95_ms via the stated formula.
status_note: Measured 2026-09-20 from a feature branch (#1082) against ad hoc local Docker containers (postgres:17-alpine + valkey/valkey:8-alpine on localhost, NOT a GitLab CI runner) — a real Postgres run with the pg_trgm indexes active, not an invented number, but explicitly NOT a CI-runner baseline per this issue's own 'a number measured on a laptop is not a CI baseline' rule. Re-derive from the first real nightly-load-test pipeline run after this MR merges (see docs/development/nightly-load-test.md#re-deriving-the-baseline) and flip status to "ci-derived" at that point.

fixture.note: --scale 20 replicates the 10-swimlane demo layout 20x (11-13 cards/swimlane, same distribution as the normal demo board) rather than picking an arbitrary target card count directly.

measurement_method.percentile_method: nearest-rank (no interpolation) over the 40 timed samples
measurement_method.auth: manage.py provision_fuzz_token --username demo2 (scoped, non-admin PAT — same mechanism backend-schema-fuzz already uses)

budget_formula: budget_p95_ms = ceil(measured_p95_ms * 1.4 / 5) * 5 -- a 1.4x factor (issue #1082 specifies 1.3-1.5x) rounded up to the nearest 5ms so CI comparisons have a little headroom for measurement noise without the number itself being picked round. Recompute this whole file -- never hand-adjust a single budget_p95_ms -- when re-deriving.

board_full.note: Serializes the entire board (all 2388 cards) in one response, unpaginated -- the most volume-sensitive endpoint in the fixture and the one this budget is least tolerant of relative headroom on, since a regression here is the one TruePPM's #2767 postmortem describes (index-shape regression, identical query count, higher latency).

card_search.note: Exercises the pg_trgm GIN indexes added in migration 0030 (card_title_trgm_idx / card_desc_trgm_idx). 'the' is a deliberately broad, high-cardinality search term -- it matches a large fraction of the corpus, closer to a real user's search-as-you-type behavior than a highly selective term would be.

card_timeline.note: Unified movement + activity feed for a single card. Exercises the comment_card_created_idx / activity_card_created_idx composite indexes added in migration 0045.

notifications_list.note: The frontend polls this every 15-30s (visiban/settings.py's DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES comment) -- the highest-QPS authenticated endpoint in the product, even though its own per-request cost is capped at 50 rows by NotificationListView.

notifications_unread.note: Companion to notifications_list -- polled at the same interval, same 50-row cap.
